classification.difficultyReason: Prove two identities with symbolic arguments and connect equal function values at reflected inputs to the axis of symmetry.

content.prompt: Consider the quadratic $f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k$ with vertex $(h,k)$. Prove the following identities and hence establish that $x=h$ is the axis of symmetry.

answer.short:
$f(h+t)=f(h-t)=at^2+k$.

Inputs equally far either side of $h$ give equal outputs, so the axis of symmetry is $x=h$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(h+t)&=a((h+t)-h)^2+k\\f(h+t)&=at^2+k\\f(h-t)&=a((h-t)-h)^2+k\\f(h-t)&=a(-t)^2+k\\f(h-t)&=at^2+k\end{align*}$$
Thus $f(h+t)=f(h-t)$ for every real $t$. The points with inputs $h+t$ and $h-t$ have the same height and lie equally far from $x=h$. Hence $x=h$ is the axis of symmetry.

answer.short:
$f(2h-x)=a(x-h)^2+k=f(x)$.

Reflection in $x=h$ sends the input $x$ to $2h-x$ and preserves the output.
answer.worked:
In part a, put $t=h-x$. Then $h+t=2h-x$ and $h-t=x$, giving $f(2h-x)=f(x)$.

Directly,
$$\begin{align*}f(2h-x)&=a((2h-x)-h)^2+k\\f(2h-x)&=a(h-x)^2+k\\f(2h-x)&=a(x-h)^2+k\\f(2h-x)&=f(x).\end{align*}$$
The inputs $x$ and $2h-x$ have midpoint $h$. Their outputs are equal, so reflection in $x=h$ leaves the graph unchanged. Hence $x=h$ is the axis of symmetry.
